label: cbbackupmgr merge command
type: the sub-command that converts two or more backups in a repository (at least one full plus incremental(s)) into a single full backup, freeing the repository of the merged-away incrementals. An Enterprise Edition command. The recommended alternative to ever taking a second full cluster backup (see backup:periodic-merge-strategy).
aliases_note: Folds a same-round self-fork, the same species as native-cloud-integration above: backup:cbbackupmgr-merge-command (2 files, the sub-command's own reference/strategy pages) and backup:merge-operation (2 files, pages discussing merging from the outside - cloud-storage compatibility, the tutorial walkthrough), zero file overlap, one mechanism. Kept under the cbbackupmgr-*-command spelling for consistency with the family of per-sub-command concepts this round minted (backup, restore, compact, remove, examine, config).
evidence: The merge command is an Enterprise Edition command which can be used to merge two or more backups together.
In order to merge data, you need to have a backup repository with at least two backups.
Doing merges should replace the full backup step by taking multiple incremental backups of a Couchbase cluster and converting them into a single full backup.
relates_to_competency_question: Can old incremental backups be consolidated into a new full backup without re-reading the whole cluster, and what does that require?
